column1: # *** THE 20 SEPTEMBER FAMILYSEARCH SESSION - three questions put, and the controls mattered more
# than two of the answers. *** Signed in again after being out since the 17th.
*** THE BRETONS WHO STOOD BY PROXY ARE NOT IN THE RECORDS BESIDE A LERENA ***
column2: Row 105. Surname *** BRETON exact *** with *** spouse surname LERENA exact ***, all countries.
column3: *** ZERO. *** Control, identical form: surname *** SALVANACH *** with spouse surname *** LERENA *** returns *** 19. *** The form works.
column4: *** A TESTED NULL, and it does not kill the lead - it narrows it. *** Jose and Maria Luisa Breton stood godparent to Roque *** by proxy *** in 1911, and proxy is what a parish writes when the sponsors are overseas. *** They did not marry into this family ***, so if they are connected it is as friends, employers or compatriots rather than kin. *** Look for them beside Lerena in Argentine records, not in marriages. ***

column1: *** ROQUE WAS BAPTISED AT FIVE AND A HALF, THREE MONTHS BEFORE HIS PARENTS MARRIED ***
column2: Row 35, read out of this archive's own files rather than off the wire.
column3: Born *** 25 Nov 1905 *** (register) or *** 6 Dec 1905 *** (death notice); baptised *** 12 June 1911 *** at Corpus Christi, Wynberg. His parents married *** 3 September 1911. ***
column4: *** SO 'CAPE TOWN' AS HIS BIRTHPLACE IS AN INFERENCE FROM WHERE HE WAS BAPTISED SIX YEARS LATER, not an attested fact ***, and the register states it flatly. *** The pattern is legitimation: *** a child baptised weeks before his parents' wedding, with his mother entered as *** 'Mary Septima olim Taylor'. *** *** Row 35's question stands open and is sharper for it - a child born in 1905 to an unmarried Argentine in the Cape could have been born anywhere. ***

column1: *** THE 1877 MARRIAGE MAY UPGRADE GILBERTO'S PARENTS FROM 'TREE' TO 'DOCUMENTED' ***
column2: Found while running the Salvanach CONTROL, not while looking for it. Marriage of *** Gilberto Lerena and Julia Salvanach, 11 August 1877, San Francisco de Asis, Ciudad Vieja, Montevideo *** - index ark 1:1:X9PV-HKCR, *** image ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-N74V-N. ***
column3: The index gives the bride's parents-in-law - that is, *** Gilberto's parents *** - as *** 'Luis Lenguas' and 'Justiniana Lenguas'. ***
column4: *** 'Luis Lenguas' is almost certainly a machine garble of LUIS LERENA, husband of JUSTINIANA LENGUAS *** - which is exactly the couple this archive already believes Gilberto Justiniano LERENA LENGUAS belongs to, *** but holds only at TREE tier. *** *** A parish marriage register would move it to DOCUMENTED. *** *** NOT CLAIMED YET: the page says 'This record was indexed by a computer', and this archive does not promote a claim on an index. Read the image. ***

column1: *** AND THE SAME INDEX CONTAINS AN OBVIOUS GARBLE, WHICH IS WHY ***
column2: The same record gives the bride *** Julia Salvanach *** a father named *** 'Cristobal Lerena' *** and a mother *** 'Angela Alvarez'. ***
column4: *** A bride surnamed SALVANACH does not have a father surnamed LERENA while marrying a Lerena. *** The two families have been crossed by the machine. *** No Cristobal Lerena is being added to this register on the strength of it *** - and the fact that one half of this record is visibly wrong is the whole argument for opening the image before trusting the other half.

column1: *** THE SANTA FE HOUSEHOLD HAS A SECOND CHILD, AND A SECOND PROVINCE ***
column2: Row 154. *** Casimiro Lerena *** with surname exact, Argentina: 7 records.
column3: *** CASIMIRO LERENA and AMELIA LEPIANI *** (indexed once as *** 'Lapriani' ***) have *** Armando Lerena *** in the Santa Fe church records and *** VENTURA AMELIA ARGENTINA LERENA *** in the *** Entre Rios *** church records.
column4: *** So this is not a Santa Fe household - it is a littoral one, in two provinces. *** *** Entre Rios is where Gilberto and Julia Salvanach's 1885 child also sits ***, so the province is worth mapping in its own right. *** Still attached to Pablo Armando by nothing whatever ***, and the only thing that ever recommended it was the forename Armando. *** That is not evidence and it is still not being treated as any. ***
